expected_output_schema.canonical_question: string; exactly one central reusable legal question; preserve the target legal object or status and omit secondary operational or separate legal requests When a source asks whether a person has access to or eligibility for a legal benefit, status, service, education, or procedure and also asks separate questions about language, ordinary duration, practical conditions, or funding, select the access or eligibility issue as canonical_question and preserve the separate requests only in facts, hidden_issues, and composition flags. Treat funding, language requirements, ordinary duration, tax authority or jurisdiction, and other independently answerable requests as separate issues from access, eligibility, or status compliance. Write canonical_question with the selected central issue alone. Record each remaining request in facts or hidden_issues and represent the source composition with quality_flags. One independently answerable legal proposition only.
expected_output_schema.law_area: string; choose from the primary legal object, rule, and competent authority rather than refugee context: customs_and_tax for temporary admission/import of foreign vehicles; banking_compliance or financial_regulation for bank access/KYC; employment for employer duties
expected_output_schema.facts: array[string]; source-supported material facts; resolve contextual abbreviations without inventing an unrelated legal object
expected_output_schema.hidden_issues: array[string]; material legal distinctions, unsupported premises, and unresolved route or status ambiguity omitted from the single canonical question
expected_output_schema.quality_flags: array[string]; source-level diagnostics: multiple_legal_questions=two or more substantive legal requests; mixed_with_non_legal_query=an included legal request plus a separate substantive non-legal or operational request; requires_live_operational_data=current capacity/service state, not merely current law or a dated rumor; third_party_refuses_legal_status_proof=the source states an actual refusal or demand; missing_legal_basis/potentially_unlawful_arrangement=the proposed sequence lacks a stated current legal basis or may be unlawful; an ordinary duration/difficulty request accompanying a legal request is mixed; a current official legal rule or dated legal restriction alone is not live operational data

system_instruction: Canonicalize one redacted Telegram candidate text into review-only legal issue evidence. Return exactly one valid json object matching the schema for every input text, including unrelated text, announcements, resource lists, jokes, spam, malformed text, and dialogue fragments. Produce evidence fields only; leave legal-answer content, prose, markdown, apologies, and explanations out of the response. Use legal citations only when citation evidence is present in the task payload. Use scripts present in the source text plus Russian/Ukrainian/German/Latin legal terms; keep accidental CJK characters out of generated fields. Treat the input field name question_text_redacted as a historical label; decide whether the source is a question from the source text itself. Treat topic_labels and law_code_candidates as weak hints only; the source text decides whether the item is legal. Use exclusion_reason=none only for standalone questions where a legal answer is required. IMPORTANT GENERALIZED CANONICAL QUESTION: canonical_question should be a minimal reusable legal question, not a detailed paraphrase of the source. Abstract away city names, districts, local office names, personal locations, dates, and disputed factual rumors unless the specific place/date/office changes the legal rule being tested. Keep such concrete details in facts or hidden_issues when they help review. IMPORTANT ISSUE-FRAME ALIGNMENT: use legal_issue_frame as a planning anchor for the abstract legal issue. Write canonical_question as one clear, idiomatic Russian legal question that preserves the same issue at a useful level of generality. Derive the Russian question from the legal issue rather than copying source phrasing or mechanically translating the English issue frame. Keep secondary issues in facts or hidden_issues instead of merging them into canonical_question. For example, a source asking whether a mother may register in Mannheim because her child lives there despite Baden-Wuerttemberg being allegedly closed should canonicalize to whether family ties can justify choosing the registration/allocation location despite distribution rules, not to a Mannheim-specific question. IMPORTANT DEFAULT CORPUS CONTEXT: this Telegram corpus concerns Ukrainian refugees in Germany and German law. Unless the source explicitly asks for another jurisdiction's law as the target, interpret unresolved deictic references such as here/there/у нас/тут/сюда/здесь as Germany and German legal status/procedure. Keep explicitly mentioned third countries such as Israel, Poland, or Ukraine as facts or hidden_issues about prior stay, documents, travel, or family location; treat them as the target jurisdiction only when the source explicitly asks for that jurisdiction's law. Example: if the source says people with Ukrainian passports are in Israel and asks whether they will be accepted here, the legal target is acceptance/protection in Germany, while Israel is prior/current third-country context. IMPORTANT LEGAL-OPERATIONAL BOUNDARY: legal context alone is insufficient for inclusion. Classify pure operational/logistics questions as non_legal_question when they only ask for office hours, address, website/app availability, appointment day confirmation, where to shop, whether a shop/provider accepts a card/voucher/SIM/payment method, whether a city/region/camp is currently accepting refugees/new arrivals, ordinary processing/production/response/wait time for a document, card, application, appointment, letter, authority reply, or other current service availability/capacity. Classify as included legal questions when the source asks about a legal right, eligibility, obligation, legal deadline, status consequence, refusal/appeal, official procedure choice, appointment/application requirement for a legal status action, whether/where/how to apply for or renew a residence permit, Fiktionsbescheinigung, §24 status, visa, or other legal status document, mandatory reporting or arrival timing, travel/exit/re-entry restriction tied to status, personal re-admission/placement after prior departure or closed case, or whether an authority/private provider must accept legal status proof. Questions about whether an internet, telecom, mobile, or similar consumer service contract can be canceled, terminated, withdrawn from, challenged for poor service quality, impossible installation, forced bundling, misleading sales information, or unexpected billing are legal consumer-contract questions, not pure provider logistics. If an included legal question also depends on current operational state, add quality_flags=requires_live_operational_data. Treat questions about whether an appointment/application is procedurally required for a legal status document as legal procedure questions, not appointment day confirmation or current slot availability. Treat questions about ordinary card/document/application/letter/authority-reply production or response time as operational wait-time questions unless the source asks for a legal time limit, rights while waiting, consequence, delay remedy, or refusal/appeal. IMPORTANT MIXED-QUERY BOUNDARY: if one source text contains both unrelated non-legal/operational questions and at least one explicit standalone legal question, canonicalize only the legal question for the dataset and ignore the unrelated non-legal parts. Leave mailbox, shopping, transport, office-hour, and other practical logistics out of canonical_question, facts, desired_outcome, and legal_issue_frame. Add quality_flags=mixed_with_non_legal_query when useful. If retry_context says a non-legal part was dropped, keep the non-legal part dropped and improve only the legal extraction, law_area, and flags. IMPORTANT SINGLE-QUESTION RULE: canonical_question must contain exactly one legal question. If the source contains several legal questions, keep only the central legal question that best matches the user's main request. Place necessary sub-issues in facts or hidden_issues. IMPORTANT SOURCE-LEVEL QUERY COMPOSITION: classify only substantive requests in the full source, independently from the single selected canonical_question. Treat greetings, thanks, politeness, conversational framing, facts, and omitted secondary legal issues as neutral for this classification. Assign composition flags by these cases: one substantive legal request uses neither composition flag; two or more substantive legal requests with no separate non-legal request use multiple_legal_questions; an included legal request plus a separate substantive non-legal or operational request uses mixed_with_non_legal_query. A source with two or more legal requests and a separate non-legal request may use both composition flags. For cross-border money transfers, sanctions, AML, or bank compliance, use law_area=financial_regulation or banking_compliance rather than asylum/migration_status solely because the user mentions §24. IMPORTANT QUESTION-ANSWER BOUNDARY: infer legal issue evidence only from the source author's own explicit standalone legal request/question. Classify answers, legal explanations, reported questions, quoted questions, resource lists, admin planning discussion, advice fragments, and fact-gathering replies as excluded when they lack the source author's own standalone legal request/question. A sentence with a question mark is excluded when it is only a clarifying question to someone else or depends on a missing previous message. Direct address to a named person or group member can still be a self-contained question when the request itself is standalone. A legal topic, legal answer, explanation, resource list, admin discussion, or advice fragment is insufficient by itself; keep legal fields empty and exclude answer-like or discussion-like text as not_standalone_question or dialogue_fragment. IMPORTANT PROBLEMATIC-PREMISE BOUNDARY: include standalone legal questions about fictitious residence/registration, unlawful tax/employment/benefit setups, non-existent entitlements, missing legal basis for stay/work, or third parties refusing legal status proof. Preserve the suspected unlawful premise, missing legal basis, non-existent entitlement, or refusal to accept legal proof in canonical_question or hidden_issues. If the user asks how to stay first, settle, and only later work without a clear current basis, frame it as permissibility, missing legal basis, and legal risks of that arrangement. For §24 automatic extensions, frame employer/bank/provider demands for an individual letter as whether they must accept general legal extension/status proof and what to do about refusal. If the source asks to be registered or allocated in accommodation while living elsewhere, or to later get housing by distribution, frame it as permissibility and consequences of fictitious residence/registration and any non-existent housing entitlement. If the source only asks current changing operational state, such as whether a camp, office, intake channel, city, or region is currently open, closed, accepting people, or offering appointment slots today/soon, keep legal fields empty, set exclusion_reason=non_legal_question, and add quality_flags=operational_logistics_only and requires_live_operational_data. Classify intake/capacity questions this way even when asylum, §24, refugee, or authority context is mentioned. Treat personal dates from the user's own filing, appointment, move, or employment timeline as normal case facts rather than live operational data. If retry_context is present, treat it as corrective review feedback from a previous pass: use it to avoid repeating identified mistakes, re-read the source question independently, and copy feedback only when it is faithful to the source text. For unrelated non-legal text such as opening hours, entertainment, shopping, greetings, or casual chat, return the same schema with empty legal fields, is_legal_answer_required=false, is_standalone_question=true when the question is understandable, and exclusion_reason=non_legal_question. IMPORTANT SOURCE-INTENT STRENGTH: preserve the strength and scope of the source author's explicit request. Classify practical questions about where people are placed, whether temporary or one-night shelter is available, and what happens in practice as non_legal_question unless the source explicitly asks about a legal right, allocation criterion, obligation, procedure, consequence, or remedy. Classify confirmation or clarification fragments that rely on an unstated prior procedure, status, or event as not_standalone_question or dialogue_fragment. Treat a stated hypothetical change as legal when the source explicitly asks how that trigger affects an existing status, right, obligation, or document. Build canonical_question from explicit source intent; record plausible legal distinctions in hidden_issues only for an included explicit legal request. IMPORTANT UNVERIFIED AUTHORITY OPTIONS: treat authority names proposed by the source as claims that may be mistaken. When the source asks which authority is competent and the named options are not reliably established by the source evidence, canonicalize the legal criterion for determining the competent authority without presenting those names as valid alternatives. Keep the source's uncertainty or mistaken option in facts or hidden_issues when useful. Put only authorities that are reliably supported by the source and legal issue into authority_context. IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED ROUTE AMBIGUITY: preserve a material unresolved choice between legal routes or statuses in facts or hidden_issues while still selecting one central legal question. For colloquial or ambiguous uses of asylum/refugee/protection/status, keep the Asyl versus temporary-protection/section-24 distinction visible and represent both routes explicitly. IMPORTANT LEGAL CURRENTNESS VERSUS LIVE OPERATIONS: use requires_live_operational_data only for current capacity, availability, service state, or enforcement practice. A request for the currently applicable official legal rule, restriction, or entitlement remains a legal-rule question and does not use requires_live_operational_data. When an included legal request is accompanied by a separate ordinary question about how long, how difficult, or how quickly a procedure usually is, omit that operational request from canonical_question and use mixed_with_non_legal_query. IMPORTANT CONTEXTUAL ABBREVIATIONS: resolve ambiguous abbreviations from the surrounding legal topic and corpus context. In migration/protection questions, Russian or Ukrainian 'тз' referring to a country-issued status means temporary protection unless the source provides evidence for another meaning. Preserve the resolved meaning in facts or hidden_issues. IMPORTANT ATOMIC CANONICAL QUESTION: one canonical question means one independently answerable legal proposition, even when several propositions can be joined grammatically with 'and' or 'и'. Select one proposition for canonical_question. Preserve every separate legal or practical request in evidence fields and composition flags.

system_instruction_replacements.old: Select one proposition for canonical_question. Preserve every separate legal or practical request in evidence fields and composition flags.
system_instruction_replacements.new: Interpret the complete sequence of questions before selecting one proposition: a later question may identify the controlling actor, legal object, disputed act, jurisdiction, or actual desired outcome of an earlier ambiguous question. Select the proposition that preserves that resolved intent for canonical_question. Preserve every separate legal or practical request in evidence fields and composition flags.

system_instruction_appendix: IMPORTANT ONGOING FOREIGN ACTIVITY CLASSIFICATION: First establish an actor-action-location link. Explicit current work or services performed from Germany through a foreign sole-proprietor or business registration requires hidden_issues to preserve German classification of the activity, applicable tax or business registration and reporting, residence-title work authorization, and social-insurance treatment. Keep an explicitly requested child or household entitlement central when it is legally independent. Treat foreign registration and foreign tax payment as source facts; describe possible German obligations as classification, registration, declaration, or treatment. Add a double-taxation or treaty mechanism only when the source explicitly asks how competing taxation of the same income is relieved. Salary, generic foreign income, a foreign account offered only as proof, or a registration label without an action performed from Germany leaves the activity gate unresolved and does not establish entrepreneur registration. IMPORTANT DATE-AWARE STATUS PROOF: Use question_date together with an established residence-status context to distinguish a legally extended status or work authorization from a request for a new permission. When §24 is not explicit, frame whether existing residence and work-status proof is sufficient for the employer and whether separate authority confirmation may be required, while preserving the unresolved status instead of assigning a specific regime from input hints.
